# Part I. SAI and PAI Physiological Analysis


This section documents the analyses conducted on the SAI and PAI physiological trajectories. The workflow proceeds from clinical outcome description to transition-feature summaries, phase-level mixed-effects models, phase-specific change-score analyses, and exploratory multilevel FPCA. Together, these analyses assess whether treatment effects are visible in scalar summaries, in phase-specific T1-T0 changes, and in latent modes of functional trajectory variation.


## Clinical Outcomes


Clinical improvement was summarized first in order to establish the behavioral context for the physiological analyses. CAPS change, IES-R total and subscale change, and STAI Y1/Y2 change were compared across conditions using descriptive summaries and between-group tests.


```{r bhi-clin-summary}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_clin_summary),
  caption = "Clinical change summaries by condition."
)
```


```{r bhi-clin-tests}
kable(
  bhi_clin_tests,
  caption = "Group comparison tests for CAPS, IES-R, and STAI change outcomes."
)
```


## Transition Feature Change Scores


The transition-feature analysis reduces each subject's curves to interpretable scalar summaries of reactivity and recovery. These change scores are then tested in two ways: between-group comparisons for treatment effects, and clinical associations with CAPS, IES-R, and STAI symptom change.


```{r bhi-transition-group}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi$transition_group_tests),
  caption = "Group comparisons for the transition-feature change scores."
)
```


```{r bhi-transition-clinical}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_transition_change_top),
  caption = "Top transition-feature associations with clinical symptom change outcomes."
)
```


```{r bhi-transition-scatterplots, fig.height=5, fig.width=7, fig.cap="Individual-level SAI/PAI transition-feature scatterplots for nominal clinical associations."}
purrr::walk(head_list(bhi$transition_clinical_scatter_plots, 6), print)
```


## Phase Summary Mixed Models


Phase-level mixed-effects models were then fit to the scalar phase summaries. For each measure and summary metric, the model evaluated the fixed effects of condition, trial, phase, and their interactions while accounting for repeated observations within participant.


```{r bhi-phase-lmm-key}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_phase_lmm_key),
  caption = "Key fixed-effect tests from the phase-summary mixed models."
)
```


## Phase-Specific Change Scores


To localize treatment-related change more directly, phase-specific T1-T0 summary-score differences were computed for each phase. These change scores were screened against CAPS, IES-R, and STAI improvement to identify whether any specific phase carried the strongest symptom-linked physiological signal.


```{r bhi-phase-clinical}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_phase_change_main),
  caption = "Top phase-specific summary-feature associations with clinical symptom change outcomes."
)
```


## Observed Subject-Level Trajectories


The following observed-data plots mirror the example trajectory figure using the actual participant curves. Each variable is shown as a 12-panel figure: TAU versus EMDR, T0 versus T1, and the three phases. Thin lines are individual participants and thick lines are group means.


```{r bhi-sai-subject-trajectories, fig.height=8.5, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Observed SAI subject-level trajectories by group, visit, and phase."}
print(bhi$subject_trajectory_plots$SAI)
```


```{r bhi-pai-subject-trajectories, fig.height=8.5, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Observed PAI subject-level trajectories by group, visit, and phase."}
print(bhi$subject_trajectory_plots$PAI)
```


## Phase-Separated T1 minus T0 Curves


The phase-separated change-curve figures display the mean T1-T0 trajectory within each phase and condition. These plots are intended as descriptive functional summaries rather than inferential tests.


```{r bhi-sai-phase-curves, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=8.5, fig.cap="SAI phase-separated T1 minus T0 curves by condition."}
print(bhi$phase_change_plots$SAI)
```


```{r bhi-pai-phase-curves, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=8.5, fig.cap="PAI phase-separated T1 minus T0 curves by condition."}
print(bhi$phase_change_plots$PAI)
```


## Phase-Wise mLFPCA


An exploratory multilevel functional principal component analysis was applied to the phase-separated SAI and PAI curves. Within each phase, the decomposition separated between-subject variation from within-subject visit-related variation. The resulting component scores were screened against CAPS, IES-R, and STAI change outcomes, while the baseline IES table is retained for continuity with the earlier draft. The strongest CAPS-related features were then entered into a regression model adjusted for condition. The final figure displays reconstructed between-subject FPCA modes for the leading principal components.


```{r bhi-mlfpca-clinical-change}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_mlfpca_change_main),
  caption = "Top SAI/PAI mLFPCA feature associations with clinical symptom change outcomes."
)
```


```{r bhi-mlfpca-scatterplots, fig.height=5, fig.width=7, fig.cap="Individual-level SAI/PAI mLFPCA scatterplots for nominal clinical associations."}
purrr::walk(bhi$mlfpca_clinical_scatter_plots, print)
```


```{r bhi-mlfpca-caps}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_mlfpca_caps_main),
  caption = "Top SAI/PAI mLFPCA feature associations with CAPS change."
)
```


```{r bhi-mlfpca-ies}
kable(
  clean_tbl(bhi_mlfpca_ies_main),
  caption = "Top SAI/PAI mLFPCA feature associations with IES at baseline."
)
```

# Part II. NerMI Valence and Motivation Analysis


This section documents the analyses conducted on the NerMI Valence and Motivation trajectories. The analytic plan combines hierarchical generalized additive modeling, fitted-trajectory visualization, CAPS-moderation analyses, and exploratory multilevel FPCA in order to characterize both mean functional structure and latent variation in the time-normalized phase trajectories.


## Observed Subject-Level Trajectories


The following observed-data plots use the same 12-panel structure as the SAI/PAI figures: TAU versus EMDR, T0 versus T1, and the three phases. Separate plots are shown for Valence and Motivation.


```{r nermi-valence-subject-trajectories, fig.height=8.5, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Observed NerMI Valence subject-level trajectories by group, visit, and phase."}
print(nermi$subject_trajectory_plots$Valence)
```


```{r nermi-motivation-subject-trajectories, fig.height=8.5, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Observed NerMI Motivation subject-level trajectories by group, visit, and phase."}
print(nermi$subject_trajectory_plots$Motivation)
```


## Joint GAMM


The primary NerMI model was a joint GAMM for Valence and Motivation. This model estimated condition-, trial-, and phase-specific functional effects across normalized within-phase time while accommodating the repeated hierarchical structure of subject, visit, and visit-by-phase observations.


```{r nermi-full-gamm-param}
kable(
  clean_tbl(nermi_full_gamm_param),
  caption = "Parametric coefficient table for the joint NerMI GAMM."
)
```


```{r nermi-full-gamm-smooth}
kable(
  clean_tbl(nermi_full_gamm_smooth),
  caption = "Smooth-term table for the joint NerMI GAMM."
)
```


## Fitted Trajectory Figures


The fitted-trajectory figures visualize the estimated curves from the joint GAMM. They include the fitted profiles themselves, a difference-in-differences functional contrast, and within-condition T1-T0 change curves.


```{r nermi-fitted-trajectories, fig.height=6, fig.width=10, fig.cap="Fitted NerMI trajectories by measure, phase, condition, and visit."}
print(nermi$plot_fitted_trajectories(nermi$pred_grid))
```



## CAPS-Moderated GAMMs


The CAPS-moderated GAMMs extend the primary NerMI model by introducing CAPS improvement as a moderator. These models test whether the shape of the Valence and Motivation trajectories varies as a function of clinical change, both through parametric interactions and through CAPS-stratified smooth terms.

```{r nermi-caps-gamm-1-param}
  clean_tbl(nermi_caps_gamm_1_param),
```

## NerMI mLFPCA


An exploratory multilevel FPCA was also performed on the phase-specific NerMI curves. As in the physiological analysis, the decomposition produced between-subject and within-subject visit-related component features. These FPCA scores were screened for association with CAPS change, the strongest features were entered into a condition-adjusted regression model, and reconstructed between-subject component curves were plotted for interpretation.


```{r nermi-mlfpca-screen}

  clean_tbl(nermi_fpca_caps_main),

)
```

# Manuscript reporting additions


## Table 1 and analytic sample


Table 1 describes the clinical change sample (EMDR n = 11, TAU n = 15), which is distinct from the 27-participant primary physiological GAMM sample.


```{r manuscript-table1}
table1 <- data.frame(
 Characteristic=c("Age, years", "Baseline CAPS-5", "Baseline IES-R", "Cancer recurrence (coded 1), n (%)"),
 EMDR=c("57.36 (7.20)","34.00 (10.84)","49.27 (15.79)","3 (27.3)"),
 TAU=c("48.40 (9.42)","33.13 (10.63)","53.27 (13.57)","1 (6.7)"))
knitr::kable(table1, caption="Baseline characteristics, clinical complete-case sample (n = 26). Continuous entries are M (SD).")
```


## Pointwise difference-in-differences confidence intervals


For each of SAI, PAI, Valence, and Motivation, pointwise 95% confidence intervals were calculated for the DiD contrast (EMDR T1 - EMDR T0) - (TAU T1 - TAU T0) from the GAMM model matrix and coefficient covariance matrix. Random-effect smooths were excluded from population-level predictions. These are pointwise, not simultaneous, intervals.


```{r manuscript-did-ci, results='asis'}
for (measure in c("pai", "sai", "nermi")) {
  file <- file.path("manuscript_gamm_ci", paste0(measure, "_did_ci.csv"))
  if (!file.exists(file)) stop("Required GAMM CI file missing: ", file)
  dat <- read.csv(file)
  stopifnot(all(c("measure","phase","time_norm","DiD","se","lower95","upper95") %in% names(dat)))
  print(knitr::kable(dplyr::summarise(dplyr::group_by(dat, measure, phase),
   n_timepoints=dplyr::n(), below_zero=sum(upper95<0), above_zero=sum(lower95>0), .groups="drop"),
   caption=paste(measure,"pointwise DiD intervals by phase")))
  fig <- file.path("manuscript_gamm_ci", paste0(measure, "_did_ci.png"))
  if(file.exists(fig)) print(knitr::include_graphics(fig))
}
```
